sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a neutral pose, showing the card face of the tabard. Panel 2: full-body true side profile, showing how thin and flat the card tabard is. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the card-back pattern of the tabard. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the head to the soles of the shoes with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: ONE officer of the Wonderland court, alone on the sheet: a man about 45 years old, a real human actor. Solid and square-shouldered, about 180 cm tall. Short grizzled hair neatly combed, a heavy grizzled moustache; grey-brown eyes; brisk, deadpan, routine expression. His livery follows the group rule, quoted verbatim from the costume bible: '1862 court ushers in Hearts livery: flat ivory playing-card tabards with crimson heart pips and corner rank indices, the backs in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette, worn over crimson wool frock coats with white piping and brass buttons, black knee breeches, white stockings and black buckled shoes; bareheaded; neat and official'. On this one officer that means he is the Eight of Hearts: the ivory card front carries exactly eight crimson heart pips in two columns of three with two between them, and a small '8' index with a small heart in the top-left and bottom-right corners. He holds a short thin white-painted usher's wand of office, about 60 cm long, upright in one hand. Bareheaded.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one officer in each panel, the same man in front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up.
